title: Checkpoint: Famous Pharaohs
objective: After this level you can compare Egypt's most famous rulers.
summary: Khufu, Tutankhamun, Seti I, Ramesses II and Cleopatra span more than two thousand years, and each is famous for something different.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 finale: Egypt’s famous rulers, and what made each one famous.
cards.body: A pyramid builder, a boy king, a father and son, and a queen who took on Rome. Put them on one line and a pattern appears.

events.label: Ramesses fights the Hittites at Kadesh

cards.headline: Fame isn’t greatness
cards.body: Each is famous for something different. Khufu is known through his pyramid, since few written sources about him remain. Tutankhamun, with little claim to fame, is famous for the tomb the robbers missed. Ramesses made himself famous with more monuments and statues than any other pharaoh, and carved a draw at Kadesh as a victory. Seti, often rated the better king, stands in his son’s shadow. Cleopatra is remembered for her struggle with Rome, lost at Actium.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 complete
learned: Khufu, Tutankhamun, Seti I, Ramesses II and Cleopatra in order
Fame came from a pyramid, a tomb, self-promotion or Rome
Abu Simbel was cut up and moved to save it

questions.prompt: Famous Pharaohs recap: on the chapter timeline, who reigned just before Ramesses II?

options.label: Khufu
options.rationale: He lived more than a thousand years earlier.

options.label: Tutankhamun
Seti I
Cleopatra VII

questions.explanation: Seti I reigned about 1290 to 1279 BCE, and his son Ramesses II took over in 1279 BCE.

questions.prompt: Famous Pharaohs recap: how were Ramesses II’s Abu Simbel temples saved in the 1960s?

options.label: A wall was built around them
options.rationale: They were moved, not walled in.

options.label: They were shipped in pieces to a museum in Europe
They were cut into blocks and rebuilt on higher ground
The Aswan High Dam was cancelled

questions.explanation: Some 16,000 blocks were moved and the temples rebuilt more than 60 metres higher.

questions.prompt: Famous Pharaohs recap: what do we know about how Tutankhamun died?

options.label: He was killed in the Battle of Kadesh
options.rationale: Kadesh was fought decades after his death.

options.label: Debated: malaria and a broken leg are suggested; none is certain
He was struck down by the mummy’s curse
He died of old age after a long and peaceful reign

questions.explanation: A 2010 study pointed to malaria with bone disease; others point to a broken leg. The case is still open.

questions.prompt: Famous Pharaohs recap: why is Ramesses II’s fame partly his own work?

options.label: He wrote Egypt’s official history books himself
options.rationale: His message was in stone, not books.

options.label: He was the only pharaoh with a tomb
He built endlessly and carved a draw at Kadesh as a victory
He ruled for only a short time

questions.explanation: More monuments and statues than any other pharaoh, and reliefs celebrating a battle that was really a draw.

questions.prompt: Famous Pharaohs recap: Level 1 said Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to one king’s monument. Which?

options.label: Tutankhamun’s tomb
options.rationale: His tomb was much closer to her time.

options.label: Khufu’s Great Pyramid
Ramesses II’s temples at Abu Simbel
options.rationale: Those were built in the New Kingdom.

options.label: Seti I’s temple at Abydos
options.rationale: That was built in the New Kingdom too.

questions.explanation: Khufu’s Great Pyramid was complete by the early 25th century BCE; Cleopatra died in 30 BCE, and the Moon landing was in 1969.
